hooks.text: In 1972, a blinding fireball streaked across the sky, never hitting ground.
How did a truck-sized space rock bounce off our atmosphere and escape?
One hundred seconds in the atmosphere before skipping back to space.

title: The Fireball That Skipped Off Earth
description: Discover the story of the 1972 Great Daylight Fireball, a massive space rock that bounced off our atmosphere and escaped back into space.

beats.text: In 1972, a blinding fireball streaked across the sky, never hitting ground.
beats.visual: Artist concept of an Earth-grazing meteoroid in the upper atmosphere, 1972

beats.text: On August 10, a truck-sized space rock entered the atmosphere over the state of Utah.
beats.visual: Map showing the trajectory of the 1972 fireball over North America, 1972
queries: Map of western United States and Canada

beats.text: Moving at 15 kilometers per second, the object glowed bright enough for people to film.
beats.visual: Diagram of atmospheric entry showing shock waves and intense heat, 1972

beats.text: Tourists in Wyoming watched the trail while a sonic boom shook the air.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Grand Teton mountain range landscape behind Jackson Lake, 1972

beats.text: Military surveillance satellites tracked the object spending 100 seconds skipping like a stone.
beats.visual: Infrared view of North America from an orbital weather satellite, 1972
queries: Weather satellite view of North America

beats.text: Instead of crashing, the meteoroid merely grazed the atmosphere and rebounded back into interplanetary space.
beats.visual: Illustration of a meteoroid skipping off the atmosphere and escaping into space, 1972

beats.text: Czech astronomer Zdenek Ceplecha determined this brief encounter permanently shifted the rock's entire orbit.
beats.visual: Orbital diagram of an Apollo-type near-Earth asteroid crossing Earth's orbit, 1994

beats.text: Not a single solid fragment reached the ground because the world only watched.
beats.visual: Close-up studio photograph of a stony meteorite specimen showing its crust, 1994
